title: Resting-ECG–peak-heart-rate interactions failed a Cleveland-to-Hungary diagnostic transport test
abstract: We tested whether resting ECG class modifies age-normalized peak exercise heart rate beyond conventional noninvasive variables and flexible additive effects. Frozen logistic models trained on303 Cleveland patients were evaluated on293 Hungarian patients from a separate clinical cohort. Adding four ECG-by-rate terms increased Brier error from0.130995 to0.142121; the joint source-refit/target-bootstrap95% interval for augmented-minus-baseline error was[-0.008519,0.047686]. Source cross-validation also worsened. A resting ST-T abnormality category had only four source observations but51 target observations, and accounted for most deterioration. Incremental value was not established. Repeated benchmark exposure, small historical referral cohorts, category shift and unavailable medication information restrict interpretation; this is not untouched confirmation or a clinical-utility study.
